subject: Physics
scope_summary: Bounded Grade-9 Pinnacle NLM production slice justified by owner-approved ExamSIDE demand: quantitative friction state/limits, common-acceleration connected bodies, and an ideal massless-string/smooth-fixed-pulley constraint. Momentum-rate, collision conservation, non-ideal pulleys and apparatus catalogues remain outside this slice.

buckets.title: Pinnacle quantitative friction and connected-body NLM
buckets.badge_reason: The main difficulty is model setup: contact state, body ownership and connection constraints must be established before quantitative equations are selected.

conventions.statement: Decide sticking, impending slip or sliding before selecting a quantitative friction relation.
Write one Newton-II equation per chosen body before eliminating internal forces or shared accelerations.
Equal tension and fixed-pulley acceleration relations require a massless inextensible string and smooth fixed pulley to be declared.

scope.covers: Quantitative static/kinetic friction conditions, common-acceleration constraints for bodies translating together, and a bounded single massless-string/smooth-fixed-pulley model with body-specific tension equations.
excluded: Massive strings, pulley rotational inertia and elastic strings.
Story-specific capabilities for each block, train, cart or incline arrangement.

capabilities.action: Choose and use the correct quantitative friction magnitude model after identifying the contact state.
capabilities.success_criterion: Distinguishes self-adjusting static friction from its limiting value and kinetic friction, obtains the normal reaction from the chosen body's perpendicular dynamics, and checks the assumed contact state against 0<=f_s<=mu_s N or the adopted kinetic model.

capabilities.action: Model bodies constrained to translate together using separate force equations and a justified common-acceleration relation.
capabilities.success_criterion: Draws or interprets one FBD per body, writes one signed Newton-II equation per body, states why the bodies share the relevant acceleration component, and solves without cancelling forces that act on different bodies.

capabilities.action: Use one massless inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley to link body-specific tension forces and endpoint accelerations.
capabilities.success_criterion: Declares the ideal connection, assigns tension arrows to the correct body FBDs, uses one tension magnitude along the same string, derives the signed fixed-length acceleration constraint, and verifies the solution in each body equation.

microtopics.title: Select a quantitative friction model from the contact state
microtopics.badge_reason: The key failure is using f=mu N automatically rather than deciding whether static friction is below limit, at limit, or the contact is sliding.
entry_assumptions: Can identify the named contact and qualitative friction direction from relative slip/tendency.
Can write a signed Newton-II component equation for one body.
microtopics.inferential_jump: The coefficient gives a bound/model, while the actual friction magnitude depends on the contact state and the normal reaction in the current geometry.

teaching_path.action: Name the contact and decide sticking, impending slip or sliding before writing a magnitude relation.
teaching_path.why_valid: The correct quantitative rule is state-dependent.

teaching_path.action: Solve the chosen body's force equation perpendicular to the contact for N.
teaching_path.why_valid: N is set by the current geometry and external forces, not by a universal N=mg rule.
teaching_path.output: Example horizontal case: N-mg=0 -> N=mg; on an incline use the perpendicular component equation instead.

teaching_path.action: For sticking use the required f_s subject to |f_s|<=mu_sN; at impending slip use |f_s|=mu_sN; during sliding use the adopted f_k=mu_kN model.
teaching_path.why_valid: This separates self-adjusting static friction from its limit and from the sliding model.
teaching_path.output: Example: required 3 N with mu_sN=8 N gives f_s=3 N, not 8 N.

teaching_path.action: Check the result against the assumed state and motion.
teaching_path.why_valid: A static result requiring more than the maximum falsifies the no-slip assumption.
teaching_path.output: If required |f_s|>mu_sN, recompute with a sliding model rather than keeping the impossible static state.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Static friction always equals mu_s N.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A 3 N horizontal push is balanced while the static-friction limit is 8 N. Is friction 8 N?
misconceptions.repair: No. Static friction supplies 3 N; 8 N is only the ceiling before slip.

misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: On an incline or with another vertical force, must N still equal mg?
misconceptions.repair: No. Solve the perpendicular force equation for the actual geometry.

exit_task.prompt: A block stays at rest under a 4 N horizontal push. The maximum static friction is 9 N. State the friction magnitude and explain why 9 N is not used.

answer.summary: Static friction is 4 N opposite the push.
reasoning: The block is sticking, so horizontal acceleration is zero.
Static friction supplies the 4 N needed for balance.
4 N is below the 9 N limit; the limiting value is not automatically active.
answer.check: The horizontal net force is zero and the required static friction satisfies the allowed bound.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The limit is used as a consistency bound, not an automatic equality.

microtopics.research_contribution: Implements the highest-priority gap identified by the merged NLM reconnaissance from repeated approved ExamSIDE friction demand.

predict.prompt: As a horizontal push grows from zero while a rough block still sticks, does static friction remain zero, jump to maximum, or adjust?
predict.defensible_answer: It adjusts to the needed value until the limiting magnitude is reached.

attempt.produces: A contact-state decision, normal reaction, state-appropriate friction magnitude and consistency check.

rubric.criterion: Does not set f_s=mu_sN unless the state is limiting.
Obtains N from actual perpendicular dynamics.

accepted: State -> N -> friction rule -> state check.
rejected: Write f=mu N before deciding whether the contact is sticking or sliding.

route.ask: What does mu_sN mean before the surfaces actually reach impending slip?
Which force equation determines N in this geometry?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Teaching presents the state-dependent relations; reconstruction starts from why unconditional f=muN fails.

boundary_test.answer: The contact is at the limiting/impending-slip boundary under this model.
boundary_test.confirms: Static equality is a boundary condition, not the default.

microtopics.title: Use a justified common acceleration without merging body ownership
microtopics.badge_reason: Learners must combine a kinematic together-motion constraint with separate Newton-II equations without cancelling interaction forces across bodies.
entry_assumptions: Can assign forces to the body on which they act and write Newton II for each selected body.
Can identify Newton-third-law partners without putting both partner forces on one FBD.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Bodies may share a constrained acceleration even though the forces and equations remain body-specific.

teaching_path.action: Draw or list one FBD for body A and one for body B, with the interaction force placed separately on each body.
teaching_path.why_valid: Newton II is applied per body; third-law partners act on different bodies.
teaching_path.output: Body A: sum(F_Ax)=m_A a_Ax; Body B: sum(F_Bx)=m_B a_Bx.

teaching_path.action: State the physical reason the bodies translate together along x: for example, maintained contact without separation or no relative slip.
teaching_path.why_valid: The common acceleration is a kinematic constraint that must come from the situation, not from Newton III.

teaching_path.action: Replace a_Ax and a_Bx by one a_common and solve the simultaneous body equations.
teaching_path.why_valid: The constraint reduces the kinematic unknowns while preserving distinct force balances.
teaching_path.output: Example pair: P-F_contact=m_A a_common; F_contact=m_B a_common.

teaching_path.action: Substitute the solved a_common and interaction force back into both equations and verify the together-motion assumption remains possible.
teaching_path.why_valid: Both dynamics and the constraint must hold at once.
teaching_path.output: Each body equation balances with the same a_common; any required friction/contact limit is also checked.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: If two bodies share acceleration, their forces must be the same.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Can two different masses share acceleration while requiring different net forces?
misconceptions.repair: Yes. Each body has F_net=m a, so equal a with different m generally means different net force.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Third-law contact forces cancel in each body's equation.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Does the A-on-B force belong on A's FBD?
misconceptions.repair: No. A-on-B acts on B; B-on-A acts on A. They only cancel when a deliberately combined system equation is formed.

exit_task.prompt: Two blocks A and B stay in contact and accelerate together on a horizontal line. An external push P acts on A. Write the minimum equation structure needed to solve their common acceleration and contact force.

answer.summary: Use one equation per block and the common-acceleration constraint.
answer.check: Substitute the solved values into both body equations; both must hold with the same acceleration.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The task checks structure and body ownership without requiring specific masses.

microtopics.research_contribution: Converts repeated approved connected-block demand into one durable common-acceleration learner action rather than apparatus-specific capabilities.

predict.prompt: If two touching blocks move together, may you cancel their contact forces inside A's individual FBD equation?
predict.defensible_answer: No. A's equation contains only the contact force acting on A.

attempt.produces: Two body-specific equations plus one justified common-acceleration constraint.

rubric.criterion: Keeps interaction forces on their correct body equations.
States why the acceleration component is shared.
rubric.evidence_of: Constraint reasoning rather than formula memorization.

accepted: Separate FBDs/equations first, then impose a_A=a_B only because the bodies translate together.
rejected: Merge both bodies before identifying the individual contact force being asked for.

route.ask: Which body receives each member of the contact-force pair?
What physical statement lets the two acceleration unknowns be replaced by one?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Teaching supplies the two-equation template; reconstruction makes the learner justify when the common acceleration is valid.

boundary_test.prompt: If one block starts slipping relative to the other or loses contact, may the common-acceleration relation still be imposed automatically?
boundary_test.answer: No. The together-motion constraint has failed and the bodies need separate kinematics.

microtopics.title: Use one ideal string and fixed pulley as a force-plus-kinematic constraint
microtopics.badge_reason: The difficult move is linking equal tension magnitude and fixed string length without treating tension partner forces as cancelling on one body.
entry_assumptions: Can solve simultaneous body-specific Newton-II equations under a previously justified acceleration constraint.
microtopics.inferential_jump: An ideal string supplies both a force-transmission statement and a kinematic length constraint; neither comes from Newton III alone.

teaching_path.action: State massless, inextensible string and smooth fixed pulley, then draw one body FBD at each endpoint.
teaching_path.why_valid: The equal-tension and fixed-length relations are model-conditional.
teaching_path.output: Body 1 has its tension T; body 2 has its own tension T along the same ideal string.

teaching_path.action: Write x_1+x_2=L for the two hanging string segments and differentiate conceptually to obtain a_1+a_2=0 in one signed convention.
teaching_path.why_valid: Inextensibility fixes the total string length, so one endpoint's increase is the other's decrease.
teaching_path.output: If + is downward on both segments: a_2=-a_1, so the magnitudes are equal for this fixed-pulley geometry.

teaching_path.action: Write one Newton-II equation per body using the same tension magnitude T and the linked accelerations.
teaching_path.why_valid: Masslessness and a smooth fixed pulley justify the shared tension magnitude along this one string.
teaching_path.output: Example hanging pair: m_1 g-T=m_1 a_1; m_2 g-T=m_2 a_2; a_1+a_2=0.

teaching_path.action: Substitute the solved T and accelerations into both body equations and the length constraint.
teaching_path.why_valid: A valid solution must satisfy dynamics and kinematics simultaneously.
teaching_path.output: Both force equations close and a_1+a_2=0 remains true.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Equal tension means the two tension forces cancel on either body's FBD.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Does the tension acting on body 2 belong in body 1's individual force sum?
misconceptions.repair: No. Equal magnitude does not change body ownership; each arrow belongs to the body it acts on.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Every pulley problem has equal tension and equal acceleration magnitudes.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Would a massive pulley or movable-pulley geometry keep the same relations?
misconceptions.repair: No. The first-slice equalities require the declared ideal fixed-pulley model and its specific length constraint.

exit_task.prompt: Two masses hang from one massless inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley. State the body equations and kinematic relation before solving.

answer.summary: Use one Newton-II equation per mass, one shared tension magnitude T, and the fixed-length relation a_1+a_2=0 in a common signed convention.
reasoning: Mass 1 contains only forces acting on mass 1, including its tension T.
Mass 2 has its own tension T from the same ideal string.
x_1+x_2=L gives a_1+a_2=0 after differentiating the fixed-length constraint.
answer.check: Any solved T,a_1,a_2 must satisfy both force equations and the length relation.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The task checks the ideal-string model and equation structure.

microtopics.research_contribution: Implements the merged reconnaissance's bounded ideal-string/fixed-pulley recommendation without creating a pulley catalogue.

predict.prompt: For one ideal fixed-pulley string, if one endpoint accelerates downward, what must the other endpoint do along the string?
predict.defensible_answer: Accelerate upward with equal magnitude in the bounded fixed-pulley geometry.

attempt.produces: Two body equations, one shared tension magnitude and one fixed-length acceleration constraint.

rubric.criterion: States the ideal-string/pulley assumptions before using equal tension.
Derives the acceleration relation from fixed string length.

accepted: Declare ideal model -> one FBD per body -> x_1+x_2=L -> a_1+a_2=0 -> solve body equations.
rejected: Use equal tension/acceleration as universal pulley facts.

route.ask: What physical property keeps x_1+x_2 constant?
Why can one T magnitude appear in both equations without cancelling the two forces?
route.why_this_ask: Separates transmission magnitude from body ownership.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Teaching gives the ideal model first; reconstruction starts from fixed length and asks the learner to recover the allowed equalities.

boundary_test.prompt: If pulley rotational inertia is significant, must the two string-side tensions remain equal?
boundary_test.answer: No. The equal-tension idealization can fail, so a different model is required.
boundary_test.confirms: This slice is explicitly bounded to a smooth ideal fixed pulley.

relations.expression: 0 <= f_s <= mu_s N; f_s,max = mu_s N; f_k = mu_k N
relations.meaning: Static friction adjusts up to a limiting magnitude; equality holds at impending slip, while the adopted kinetic model is used after sliding is established.
conditions: The contact pair and relative sliding/tendency have been identified.
The normal reaction N belongs to that same contact in the current force state.
Use f_s = mu_s N only at the limiting/impending-slip state; otherwise static friction may be smaller.
Use f_k = mu_k N only when the adopted kinetic-friction model applies during relative sliding.

derivation.action: Classify the contact as sticking, limiting or sliding and identify friction direction from slip/tendency.
derivation.why_valid: The magnitude model depends on contact state, not merely on the presence of a coefficient.

derivation.action: Solve the perpendicular Newton-II equation for N before evaluating a friction bound/model.
derivation.why_valid: The current geometry and other forces determine N.
derivation.output: For a horizontal surface with no other vertical force and a_y=0: N-mg=0, so N=mg; for other geometries solve the actual perpendicular equation.

derivation.action: Use the static bound/limit or kinetic relation and test whether the assumed contact state remains possible.
derivation.why_valid: A required static friction above mu_s N falsifies sticking.
derivation.output: Example consistency test: required f_s=3 N with limit 8 N is allowed; required f_s=10 N is not.

limits: The proportional dry-friction model is an idealization, not a universal material law.
Static friction is not automatically equal to its maximum.
checks: A sticking solution must satisfy |f_s|<=mu_s N.
The friction direction must oppose relative sliding or the tendency to slide.

relations.expression: For bodies constrained to translate together along x: a_Ax = a_Bx = a_common
relations.meaning: A no-separation/no-slip translational constraint can link the relevant acceleration component of multiple bodies while Newton II still applies separately to each body.

symbols.meaning: Signed acceleration component of body A along the constrained direction
Signed acceleration component of body B along the constrained direction
Shared signed acceleration component implied by the translation constraint

conditions: The bodies are constrained to remain in contact or otherwise translate together along the stated direction during the interval.
Each Newton-II equation is written for one chosen body in one consistent signed axis.
The common-acceleration equality applies only to the constrained component; other components are not silently equated.

derivation.action: Choose body A and body B separately and write the forces acting on each.
derivation.why_valid: Force ownership remains body-specific even when kinematics are linked.
derivation.output: Body A: sum(F_Ax)=m_A a_Ax; Body B: sum(F_Bx)=m_B a_Bx.

derivation.action: If the stated contact/connection keeps the bodies translating together, impose a_Ax=a_Bx=a_common.
derivation.why_valid: The geometric/contact constraint links motion, not Newton III itself.
derivation.output: Replace both acceleration unknowns by one a_common only after the constraint is justified.

derivation.action: Substitute the solved a_common and interaction force back into both body equations.
derivation.why_valid: A valid solution must satisfy each body's Newton-II equation and preserve the assumed together-motion condition.
derivation.output: Both residual force equations evaluate to zero with the same a_common.

limits: Do not impose equal acceleration if bodies can slip, separate or move through a different connection geometry.
Equal acceleration is a kinematic constraint, not a Newton-third-law statement.
checks: Each interaction force appears only on the FBD of the body it acts on.
The solved acceleration must be identical in the constrained component for all bodies declared to move together.

relations.expression: Same ideal string: T_1 = T_2 = T; fixed-pulley length constraint x_1 + x_2 = constant gives a_1 + a_2 = 0
relations.meaning: A massless inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley transmits one tension magnitude along the same string while its fixed length links endpoint motions.

symbols.meaning: Tension magnitude along one continuous ideal string
Signed endpoint displacement along one string segment
Signed endpoint displacement along the other string segment
Signed endpoint acceleration along the first string segment
Signed endpoint acceleration along the second string segment

conditions: The string is massless and inextensible.
The pulley is smooth and fixed.
The same continuous string is being referenced when one tension magnitude T is used.

For the bounded fixed-pulley geometry, total string length is constant so the two endpoint acceleration components along the string have equal magnitude and opposite sign in one common signed convention.

derivation.action: Draw one FBD per body and label the tension force T on the body on which each arrow acts.
derivation.why_valid: Equal tension magnitudes do not mean the two force arrows belong on one FBD.
derivation.output: Body 1 equation contains its T arrow; Body 2 equation contains its own T arrow.

derivation.action: For one massless string over a smooth fixed pulley, use T_1=T_2=T and x_1+x_2=L.
derivation.why_valid: Masslessness/smooth redirection support one tension magnitude; inextensibility fixes total string length.
derivation.output: Differentiate the length constraint twice in the chosen signs: a_1+a_2=0.

derivation.action: Solve the two body equations with the string constraint, then substitute T and accelerations back.
derivation.why_valid: The dynamic equations and fixed-length kinematics must be simultaneously satisfied.
derivation.output: Example structure: sum(F_1)=m_1 a_1; sum(F_2)=m_2 a_2; a_2=-a_1; one shared T.

limits: Massive strings or pulley rotational inertia can produce unequal tensions.
Movable-pulley geometries can produce acceleration ratios other than one-to-one and require a separately derived length constraint.
checks: Every tension arrow must be attached to the body it acts on.
The endpoint accelerations must satisfy the declared fixed-length relation.

teaching_routes.title: Reveal bounded quantitative-friction and connected-body slice
entry_needs: Core FBD ownership, Newton II, qualitative friction and Newton III are available.
learner_actions: Choose friction state before magnitude relation.
Use separate body equations plus a justified common acceleration.
Use ideal-string/fixed-pulley tension and length constraints.
help_plan: Ask whether the contact is sticking/sliding before muN.
Keep one body per equation until interaction forces are identified.
Write the string-length relation before asserting endpoint acceleration equality.
teaching_routes.reveal_plan: Each quantitative relation is introduced only after its physical state/constraint is declared, then verified against the original model.

source_preferences.reason: Approved ExamSIDE questions repeatedly require friction thresholds and connected/string/pulley setup.

when_not_suitable: Do not extend into momentum-rate recoil, collisions, massive strings, pulley inertia or movable/compound pulley catalogues in this slice.

teaching_routes.title: Reconstruct bounded friction/connected-body model choices
entry_needs: Learner can commit to contact state, body boundary or connection assumption before formula reveal.
learner_actions: Explain why static friction may be below its maximum.
Justify a shared acceleration from together-motion.
Derive fixed-pulley endpoint relation from string length.
help_plan: Ask what keeps the bodies moving together.
Ask what quantity stays constant for an inextensible string.
teaching_routes.reveal_plan: Prediction and constraint reconstruction precede closed equations.

source_preferences.reason: The question bank varies apparatus while preserving the same contact and connection invariants.

when_not_suitable: Do not create new capabilities for a different incline angle, block count or story if the same invariant decisions solve it.
